# Evaluating SAE Features Without Explanations as a Cheap Safety Audit

**Problem:** Standard SAE evaluation relies on auto-generated natural-language explanations of features, which are expensive and themselves error-prone. A 2025 line proposes evaluating SAE interpretability WITHOUT explanations, but it has not been applied as a triage tool to flag which safety-relevant features are actually trustworthy.

**Direction:** Take a public SAE, identify candidate safety-relevant features by activation patterns (toxicity, refusal), and apply explanation-free interpretability metrics (e.g., activation-prediction consistency, intervention coherence) to rank which features are reliable enough to monitor. Validate the ranking against a small manual inspection.

**Why it matters:** Gives facilitators and small labs a cheap, training-free triage method to decide which SAE features to trust for monitoring, directly addressing the SAE-reliability gap without proprietary infrastructure.

**Relevant context:** 'Evaluating SAE interpretability without explanations' (arXiv 2507.08473) proposes explanation-free metrics. SAELens/Neuronpedia host public SAEs with feature dashboards but no standardized safety evaluation (identified benchmark gap).
